correctness.rationale: Stationary fractions are derived by reset-age Laplace transforms and independently exact-checked against CTMC balance equations. At each of \(n-1\) separated forward rates two adjacent masses exceed 0.49, yielding Simpson >0.48 and Shannon >=Simpson; at each intervening geometric-mean intensity one stage has mass >=1-1/(100n), yielding Simpson <0.01 and Shannon <0.105. Real analyticity and low end limits force \(n-1\) distinct strict interior peaks, robust to rate perturbations. For three stages the exact derivative is a rational multiple of a quartic; its discriminant is \(4r^2F(r)\). Two integer-polynomial interval transforms are strictly negative below 12, and a one-sign-change shift above 12 proves the unique positive discriminant threshold. Exact sign brackets at r=20 establish the post-threshold three-positive-root regime. The packaged pure-Python verification code passed 49 exact CTMC/product comparisons, 245 inequality checks, all sign certificates and 15 exact Sylvester-determinant polynomial-identity specializations; finite checks are supplementary, not substitutes for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The intermediate-disturbance hypothesis predicts a diversity peak and Johst–Huth exhibited two; the natural quantitative gap is how peak number grows with the number of successional stages. This finding removes every global bound on the number of peaks in a standard homogeneous-reset Markov ecology model, establishes a robust explicit family for two distinct diversity indices, proves the smallest stage count for bimodality, and gives a nontrivial necessary-and-sufficient three-stage rate threshold of polynomial degree seven. It is a structural response-shape result rather than a numerical recomputation, while ecological applicability is limited by strong transition-rate separation and stage diversity versus species diversity.
